title: Miamegg (Jamesport Creek)
summary: Miamegg is a Jamesport creek placename connected with a 1648 deed and interpreted as a meeting fishing-place.
address_label: Kings Creek / Hawks Creek, South Jamesport, Riverhead, NY (approximate waterway orientation)
map_geometry_source: Approximate waterway point at Kings Creek/Hawks Creek in South Jamesport, supported by Tooker entry 192 and federal dredging records; the historic channel identification is not treated as exact.
introduction_content: Miamegg names a creek near Jamesport in Riverhead town. Related forms include Miamogue, Miomog, and Wyamaug, with later sources sometimes shifting the name from the creek to the nearby point.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a meeting fishing-place, a locality where people came together to fish, probably for alewives or menhaden used for food and planting.

Why Place Names Matter

“The white man’s influence is seen also in the introduction of names from other and kindred Indian tongues, and in the “invention” or “improvement” of such.”

— Alexander F. Chamberlain, The Indian Place-Names on Long Island and Islands Adjacent, with Their Probable Significations (1911), Introduction by Alexander F. Chamberlain, p. xii
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: The pin is placed near Jamesport and Peconic Bay to represent the creek named in relation to Assasquage. It is moved slightly from Assasquage so each can be seen and is not an exact surveyed creek point.
